_readme: Design briefs for the recurring-revenue business specialist program (user request, 2026-08-12).
Each business becomes ONE FACTORY vertical: FACTORY/recurring_revenue/<slug>/ holding
3 compact KB content-specs (forged + gated dense 35/35) and 1 specialist (gated 13/13),
built exactly per FACTORY/MAKE_A_SPECIALIST.md Path B and FACTORY/build.sh.
The 3-KB decomposition per business follows one lens, named domain-specifically:
KB1 = acquisition & offer economics, KB2 = delivery & installation/service operations,
CONTENT HONESTY RULES (apply to every KB and specialist; extends docs/EXPANSION_PLAN.md section 4
and the FACTORY neutralize lane): (1) no fabricated firm figures - commissions, prices, rates and
account multiples are described as MECHANISMS or qualitative bands, never invented numbers stated as
fact; (2) licensing/regulatory points name the obligation class and flag 'verify current rules in
your jurisdiction' rather than asserting specifics; (3) educational, not personalized financial,
legal, tax, medical or insurance advice; (4) sales content must encode ethical-selling constraints
(disclosure, no fear-selling, vulnerable-consumer care) as first-class nodes/rules, not afterthoughts.

businesses.label: Home Security & Alarm Dealer
businesses.money_model: sell/install monitored security systems (alarm, doorbell, cameras); revenue = equipment + installation fee + recurring monitoring/support account
boundaries: defensive, lawful security only - systems exist to prevent, detect and alarm intrusions
low-voltage/alarm licensing and permit rules vary by state and city - flag 'verify locally', never assert specifics
alarm contracts are consumer-protection sensitive: auto-renewal, term and cancellation terms must be disclosed honestly
dealer-program economics (subsidies, account multiples, holdbacks) described as mechanisms, never invented figures

kbs.scope: Choosing between authorized-dealer programs and the independent model; how a monitored account is created and funded (equipment subsidy vs margin, monitoring wholesale vs retail spread, account sale vs hold decisions, holdback/chargeback mechanisms); territory and segment targeting; lead generation and ethical in-home selling for security.

Site survey and risk walk-through; designing the panel/sensor/doorbell/camera package to the home and threat model; installation quality and testing; permits, false-alarm ordinances, licensing awareness; subcontract vs in-house install trade-offs.

Central-station vs self/cloud monitoring stack choice; building recurring monthly revenue through monitoring + cloud video + service plans; attrition drivers and retention playbook; contract hygiene and honest renewal practice; what determines the value of a monitored-account book.

businesses.label: Merchant Processing / POS Agent
businesses.money_model: acquire merchants (restaurants, salons, c-stores, mechanics); place/arrange POS and card acceptance; revenue = POS sale/lease + share of processing economics; the durable asset is the book of merchants
boundaries: no deceptive rate-comparison or 'we'll definitely save you X%' claims - statement analysis is a diagnostic mechanism, savings are verified per merchant
interchange, markup and residual splits described as mechanisms, never invented percentages stated as fact
card-network rules, PCI-DSS and surcharging law are compliance classes to flag, jurisdiction- and network-specific
not financial or legal advice; merchant underwriting decisions belong to the processor

kbs.scope: Selecting ISO/agent programs and what their agreements actually govern; choosing and winning merchant verticals; the bundle-led sales strategy (POS + phones + internet + cameras + support as one relationship); honest statement analysis; compliant sales claims.

Matching POS hardware/software to the vertical; the application/underwriting/KYC path and what delays or kills it; installation, menu/catalog build, staff training; PCI scope basics at deployment; go-live support.

How residual streams are computed and paid as mechanisms; attrition drivers and merchant-level margin health; support economics; chargeback education for merchants; cross-sell leverage from the trusted-operator position; portfolio valuation and sale/retention decisions.

businesses.label: Business VoIP Reseller
businesses.money_model: sell/configure business phone systems, port numbers, provide monthly service; revenue = hardware/setup + installation + monthly per-seat service + ongoing support; targets: dentists, trucking, restaurants, motels, small offices
boundaries: E911 obligations (Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class of rules) are a hard compliance flag on every deployment - verify current requirements, never skip
telecom regulatory/tax treatment (USF-class obligations) varies by model (agent vs reseller) - flag for professional verification
agent/reseller/white-label economics described as mechanisms, never invented commission figures
no guaranteed-uptime or savings claims without a verified basis

kbs.scope: Agent vs reseller vs white-label models and who owns the customer, the bill and the risk; picking vertical niches (dentists, trucking, restaurants, motels, offices) and their phone-system pain; packaging hardware + setup + monthly service + support into one offer; honest competitive positioning.

kbs.domain_label: VoIP Deployment, Number Porting & Call Quality
kbs.scope: Needs assessment and seat/feature mapping; phones vs softphones vs existing-device reuse; the number-porting process and its failure modes (the business number is the crown jewel); network readiness, QoS and failover; E911 configuration; cutover planning and training.

Running the MRR base: support model and escalation to the carrier/platform; churn signals and prevention; seat and feature expansion; contract/SLA hygiene and honest renewals; periodic account reviews that surface cross-sell (internet, cameras, Wi-Fi) without overreach.

businesses.label: Business Internet & Wireless Agent
businesses.money_model: sell business internet, backup 5G/wireless and related services through carrier agent/partner programs; revenue = activation + ongoing/account-based compensation; strongest when bundled (internet + backup + Wi-Fi + phones + cameras)
boundaries: carrier partner-program terms, compensation plans and product availability change - always verify the current program before any commitment
compensation structures described as mechanisms (activation vs residual vs account-based), never invented figures
serviceability is address-specific fact-finding, never assumed
no misrepresentation of carrier affiliation; the agent sells the carrier's service under the program's rules

kbs.scope: How carrier agent/partner/reseller programs differ (who bills, who supports, who owns the account); qualifying and selecting programs; the multi-service bundle strategy that makes one small-business customer several revenue streams; account planning and honest needs discovery.

Serviceability and coverage checks per address; site survey for primary + wireless-backup design; ordering, provisioning and activation coordination with the carrier; failover configuration and testing; install handoff to the customer and to any bundled services.

Tracking activation vs ongoing compensation as program mechanisms; renewals, upgrades and technology refresh cycles; churn and win-back; being the escalation layer between customer and carrier; growing multi-stream accounts and protecting compensation through program compliance.

businesses.label: CCTV & Cloud Video Recording
businesses.money_model: own-build vertical (not a major-company agent): camera installation + cloud recording/support subscription; revenue = install + monthly cloud storage/monitoring/support per site
boundaries: lawful, disclosed surveillance only - no covert or unlawful monitoring; purpose is deterrence, detection and evidence for the property owner
video privacy, audio-recording consent and camera-placement law vary sharply by jurisdiction - flag 'verify locally' on every design
retention and access policy is a first-class design decision, not an afterthought
VSaaS platform vs own-stack economics as mechanisms; no invented per-camera price points stated as fact

kbs.scope: Productizing camera + cloud recording + support into subscription tiers; segment targeting (retail, restaurants, contractors, small industrial, residential); build-on-VSaaS-platform vs own-stack decision; pricing architecture as mechanism (hardware margin vs subscription margin); ethical selling without fear-mongering.

Site survey and coverage design (entrances, POS, yards, blind spots); camera selection and placement; recording architecture (edge vs cloud vs hybrid) and bandwidth/storage math as mechanisms; network segmentation and hardening of cameras; installation quality, cabling and commissioning tests.

Running the recurring service: camera-health monitoring, storage/retention management, incident retrieval workflow; privacy/consent compliance and signage; access control and audit of who views footage; subscription retention, service plans and honest renewals; churn drivers for camera subscriptions.

businesses.label: GPS / Fleet Tracking Reseller
businesses.money_model: sell/install GPS trackers to fleets and equipment owners; revenue = tracker hardware + monthly tracking-platform subscription per unit
boundaries: lawful tracking only: owner/employer-authorized vehicles and assets, with required employee disclosure - covert tracking of private individuals is out of scope
ELD/hours-of-service and telematics-privacy rules are jurisdiction- and fleet-type-specific - flag for verification
platform reseller economics as mechanisms, never invented per-unit figures

kbs.scope: Target fleets (trades, delivery, trucking, equipment rental) and their loss/efficiency pain; platform-reseller vs white-label economics; hardware-plus-subscription offer design; ROI-based ethical selling grounded in the customer's own numbers, not invented savings.

Device selection (OBD, hardwired, battery asset trackers) per use case; installation and concealment-vs-serviceability trade-offs; platform account setup, geofences, alerts and reports configured to the fleet's workflow; driver-disclosure onboarding; verification testing per unit.

Per-unit MRR management; monitoring device health and data quality; renewal and contract hygiene; expanding within an account (more vehicles, assets, dashcams, maintenance modules); churn signals for fleet accounts; support economics at unit scale.

businesses.label: Managed Wi-Fi Provider
businesses.money_model: design/install business Wi-Fi (router/APs) + monthly management, monitoring and support subscription; venues: restaurants, motels, offices, retail, multi-tenant
boundaries: guest-network privacy: no traffic interception or sale of user data; captive-portal data collection must be disclosed
managed-service pricing as mechanism (per-AP / per-site tiers), never invented figures
spectrum/wiring and code constraints are site-specific facts to survey, not assumptions

kbs.scope: Productizing Wi-Fi-as-a-service (design + hardware + monthly management) per venue type (restaurant, motel, office, retail, MDU); guest vs operations network value propositions; per-AP/per-site subscription architecture as mechanism; positioning against one-time installers.

RF site survey and AP placement; SSID/VLAN segmentation (guest vs POS vs back-office); hardware platform selection with cloud management; captive portal setup and disclosure; installation, cabling and validation testing; documentation handoff.

Remote monitoring and alerting; proactive maintenance and firmware hygiene; SLA design and honest uptime reporting; support tiers and escalation; renewal/retention of management subscriptions; expansion to additional sites and adjacent services (cameras, VoIP).

businesses.label: Website & Hosting Reseller
businesses.money_model: build small-business websites + recurring hosting/maintenance/care plans; revenue = site build fee + monthly hosting, updates, backups, edits
boundaries: client owns their domain and content - lock-in through service quality, never through hostage-holding of assets
care-plan pricing as mechanism/tiers, never invented market rates
no SEO/traffic guarantees; performance claims must be verifiable

kbs.scope: Productizing site-build + care-plan offers for local small businesses; niche selection and referral-loop acquisition; scoping and expectation-setting that prevents scope creep; honest positioning on what a website can and cannot do for a business.

Choosing a repeatable build stack; the standardized build pipeline (content intake, design system, build, review, launch); quality/performance/accessibility baseline; domain/DNS/email handling without breaking the client's business; launch checklist.

Hosting architecture for a portfolio of small sites; backup/update/security operations; care-plan tiers and what each honestly includes; monthly reporting that proves value; retention, reactivation and graceful offboarding with full asset handover.

businesses.label: Business Email & Cloud Reseller
businesses.money_model: set up and manage Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace and adjacent cloud subscriptions for small businesses; revenue = setup/migration fees + monthly per-seat margin/management
boundaries: client data handled under least-privilege and documented authorization; admin access is a fiduciary-grade responsibility
partner-program (CSP-class) margin structures as mechanisms - terms change, verify current program
no fear-based upselling of licenses the client does not need

kbs.scope: How indirect-reseller/partner programs work (who bills, margin as mechanism, support obligations); picking the anchor suite; SMB segments with acute email/collaboration pain; the trusted-IT-operator wedge positioning; right-sizing license mix ethically.

Tenant architecture and security baseline (MFA, admin separation, backup); mail/data migration planning and cutover without business interruption; DNS/domain integrity; user onboarding and training; documentation of the delivered environment.

Monthly seat/license administration and true-ups; support model and boundaries; security posture reviews as recurring value; renewal management; expansion paths (backup, security add-ons, device management) driven by need, not quota; churn prevention.

businesses.label: Managed Cybersecurity Services
businesses.money_model: package security stack (endpoint protection, patching, backup, awareness, monitoring) for small businesses; revenue = setup/hardening project + monthly per-seat/per-site subscription
boundaries: strictly defensive scope: protect, detect, respond for the authorized client - no offensive services, no unauthorized testing
written authorization and scope definition precede any security work
no absolute-protection claims - security reduces risk, never eliminates it; honest incident communication
compliance framework mapping is guidance, not certified audit or legal advice

kbs.scope: Packaging a defensible SMB security stack into tiers; risk-conversation selling without fear-mongering (threat literacy, not scare tactics); qualifying clients and setting scope/authorization; cyber-insurance-driven demand as an honest wedge; pricing architecture as mechanism.

Selecting and deploying the stack (endpoint protection, patch management, backup/recovery, MFA, email filtering, awareness training); the initial hardening project and its acceptance tests; asset inventory as foundation; documenting the security baseline delivered.

Ongoing monitoring/alert triage at SMB scale; incident-response runbook and honest client communication during incidents; backup verification and recovery drills; recurring security reviews and reporting that prove value; retention and scope-growth of the security subscription.

businesses.label: Life Insurance Agent
businesses.money_model: licensed agent selling life products; revenue = policy commissions + renewal/trail compensation depending on product and carrier; the durable asset is a persistent, well-served book
boundaries: state insurance licensing is mandatory before any solicitation - jurisdiction-specific, verify current requirements
educational and process knowledge, not personalized financial or insurance advice; suitability rules govern recommendations
no performance promises on cash-value products; illustrations are projections, not guarantees
replacement regulations and disclosure duties are compliance classes to flag; commission structures as mechanisms, never invented percentages

kbs.scope: The licensing path and continuing obligations as requirement classes; captive vs independent vs IMO-affiliated models and who owns the book; carrier/product-shelf selection; choosing a market focus (families, business owners, final expense) and lead-generation ethics.

Fact-finding and needs analysis; term vs permanent product mechanics as mechanisms; matching product to need under suitability and best-interest standards; the application, underwriting and delivery process; honest illustration handling and replacement discipline.

Why persistency is the economic engine (chargebacks, renewals, trails as mechanisms); service cadence that keeps policies in force; policy reviews and life-event triggers; referral systems; building a book that compounds rather than churns.

businesses.label: Property & Casualty Insurance Agent
businesses.money_model: licensed P&C agent selling auto/home/business policies; revenue = new-business + renewal commissions; renewal book is the asset
boundaries: P&C licensing is mandatory and state-specific - verify current requirements
educational, not personalized insurance advice; coverage recommendations follow documented needs analysis
no premium-savings guarantees; quotes are carrier-determined
commission and contingency structures as mechanisms, never invented figures; E&O exposure is a first-class risk to manage

kbs.scope: Licensing and appointment requirement classes; captive vs independent agency economics and book ownership; carrier access paths for new agencies (direct appointments, aggregators/clusters as mechanisms); market focus selection across personal and small-commercial lines.

Risk intake and honest application accuracy; coverage design for auto/home/small-business (limits, deductibles, exclusions as decision mechanisms); multi-carrier quoting and proposal ethics; binding, documentation and E&O-safe process discipline.

Renewal-cycle management and remarketing decisions; retention economics vs new-business economics as mechanisms; claims-time service as the loyalty event; cross-sell/account-rounding done from need; what drives agency-book valuation and transferability.

businesses.label: Health / Medicare Insurance Agent
businesses.money_model: licensed, certified agent enrolling clients in Medicare-related and health plans; revenue = enrollment compensation + renewals under regulated schedules
boundaries: the most regulated vertical in this set: CMS marketing/communication rules, annual certification (AHIP-class) and carrier certifications are hard prerequisites - compliance dominates growth in every conflict
educational, not personalized plan advice; enrollment decisions belong to the beneficiary
no steering by compensation; plan comparison must be need-driven and documented
compensation is set by regulated schedules - describe as mechanism, verify current-year rules; senior clients are a protected/vulnerable population - ethical-contact rules are first-class

kbs.scope: The certification/appointment stack as requirement classes (license, annual certification, carrier contracts); CMS marketing-rule classes (permission to contact, scope of appointment, prohibited practices); compliant lead generation and community presence; documentation habits that survive audits.

kbs.domain_label: Enrollment Periods, Plan Comparison & Needs Fit
kbs.scope: The enrollment-period system as the demand calendar (initial, annual, special classes); need-driven plan comparison (coverage types as mechanisms: original-plus-supplement vs advantage-class trade-offs, drug coverage fit, provider networks); the compliant enrollment conversation and its required artifacts.

Renewal-compensation mechanics as regulated mechanisms; year-round service model (plan changes, provider issues, drug-cost events); annual-review practice under marketing rules; retention through service quality, not pressure; book stability and compliant growth via referrals.

businesses.label: Medical Alert Systems
businesses.money_model: sell/set up personal emergency response devices for seniors; revenue = device + monthly monitoring subscription
boundaries: not medical advice or a medical device consultation - it is emergency-signaling equipment plus monitoring service
seniors and their families are a vulnerable-consumer population: transparent pricing, easy cancellation, no scare-selling - these are first-class rules
reliability claims (battery, range, response time) must be device-verified, not asserted; testing protocol is mandatory at setup
monitoring economics as mechanisms, never invented figures

kbs.scope: The buyer triangle (senior user, adult-child payer, care professionals as referrers); referral-channel building (home care, senior centers, discharge planners) done ethically; transparent offer design; vulnerable-consumer sales rules as hard constraints; honest competitive positioning.

Device-type selection (in-home vs mobile/GPS, fall-detection class capabilities honestly framed); home assessment (range, connectivity, mounting); monitoring-center integration and emergency-contact tree setup; the mandatory end-to-end signal test and user training; documentation.

Running the monitoring subscription: periodic test-call cadence, battery/device health, address/contact currency; family/caregiver communication; churn realities (moves to higher care, passing of the user) handled with dignity and easy cancellation; service recovery after missed signals; referral loops from well-served families.

businesses.label: Home Warranty / Service Plan Sales
businesses.money_model: sell home service contracts/warranty plans; revenue = contract commissions + renewals
boundaries: service contracts are state-regulated products (registration/obligor rules vary) - verify jurisdiction before selling
exclusions, caps and claim conditions MUST be surfaced before sale - burying them is the vertical's core ethical failure
the agent sells a defined contract, not a promise that everything is covered; claims outcomes belong to the obligor
commissions as mechanisms, never invented figures

kbs.scope: How home-warranty/service-plan products are structured (obligor, administrator, term, caps as mechanisms); distribution channels (realtor/closing, direct-to-homeowner, property managers, trade partnerships); channel economics and compliance classes per channel.

Reading and explaining a contract: covered systems, exclusions, caps, waiting periods, pre-existing-condition clauses as decision mechanisms; the disclosure-first sales conversation; matching plan tier to the home's realistic risk profile; documentation that protects both client and seller.

Renewal economics and honest renewal conversations; being the client's guide (not the obligor's shield) during claims; managing the reputation risk of a claims-denial-prone product class; retention through set-expectations-right selling; when to advise a client a plan is not worth renewing.

businesses.label: Payroll Service / Referral Business
businesses.money_model: acquire small-business payroll clients (referral partnership with a payroll platform, or run a service practice on top of one); revenue = referral/revenue-share + recurring per-client relationship
boundaries: payroll tax filing is a compliance-critical professional domain - errors carry penalties; not tax or legal advice
referral/revenue-share structures as mechanisms - verify current partner-program terms
client data (SSNs, wages, banking) demands strict confidentiality and least-privilege handling

kbs.scope: Referral-partner vs reseller vs service-bureau-on-platform models and their obligations; who refers payroll well (bookkeepers, CPAs, insurance agents, associations); the switching-pain sales reality (payroll changes happen at year/quarter boundaries); honest platform selection for the client.

The onboarding project: entity/tax-account setup classes, employee data migration, year-to-date balances, direct-deposit setup; parallel-run verification before cutover; the compliance calendar handoff; setting service boundaries between platform, service layer and client.

The recurring service rhythm (per-run checks, quarter/year-end classes of filings as calendar mechanisms); issue triage between client and platform; retention through error-free runs; expansion into adjacent recurring services (bookkeeping, HR add-ons, benefits referrals) driven by need.

businesses.label: Subscription Bookkeeping Practice
businesses.money_model: monthly bookkeeping/accounting packages for small businesses; revenue = fixed monthly subscription per client tier
boundaries: bookkeeping, not attest/audit work and not tax or legal advice; know where licensed-CPA territory begins - flag it
fixed-fee tiers as pricing mechanisms; no invented market rates
client financial data confidentiality and access discipline are first-class

kbs.scope: Designing fixed-fee monthly tiers (scope per tier as mechanism); niche selection (trades, e-commerce, restaurants, professional services) and why niching compounds; qualification and scope-discipline at sale; positioning against hourly bookkeeping and DIY software.

The diagnostic review and cleanup/catch-up project as the entry gate; chart-of-accounts and workflow standardization; the repeatable monthly close checklist (feeds, reconciliation, categorization review, reporting packet); accuracy controls and escalation of judgment calls to the client or their CPA.

Practice economics as mechanisms (clients-per-seat capacity, scope-creep control, repricing cadence); retention through reporting the owner actually reads; monthly-review conversations; handling seasonal/at-risk clients; when and how to fire a mis-fit client; referral engines with CPAs and niche communities.

businesses.label: Tax Preparation Practice
businesses.money_model: per-return fees with an annually returning client base; seasonal peak with off-season extension/amendment/planning work
boundaries: preparer registration/credential classes (PTIN/EFIN-class requirements, state rules) are prerequisites - verify current rules
process and practice knowledge, not tax advice for specific situations; accuracy and penalty exposure make verification non-negotiable
no refund-size promises or aggressive-position selling; due-diligence obligations on credits are compliance classes to respect

kbs.scope: Credential/registration requirement classes and software/e-file infrastructure; choosing a client segment (individual, small-business, niche) and service model (office, virtual, hybrid); the seasonal demand curve as the practice's economic mechanism; pricing architecture per return complexity.

The per-return pipeline (intake, document collection, preparation, review, sign/file) built for peak-season throughput without accuracy loss; error classes and their controls; due-diligence documentation habits; handling ambiguity (research, escalate, decline); data security for the most sensitive client data class.

What makes clients return annually (experience, proactivity, trust) as retention mechanisms; post-season follow-up and next-year positioning; off-season lines (extensions, amendments, quarterly estimates, planning-adjacent education, bookkeeping cross-over); capacity smoothing and referral growth.

businesses.label: Commercial Cleaning Broker
businesses.money_model: win commercial cleaning contracts, arrange service through crews/subcontractors, retain the monthly margin
boundaries: employee-vs-independent-contractor classification is a legal risk class that varies by jurisdiction - flag for professional verification, never assume
honest broker positioning: the client knows the service model; no misrepresentation of who cleans
margin structures as mechanisms, never invented figures; insurance/bonding requirement classes verified per contract

kbs.scope: Target facility classes (offices, medical, retail, industrial) and their buying process; walkthrough-based scoping; bid construction as mechanism (labor-load math from square footage/frequency/task list); proposal and contract terms that protect margin; honest differentiation.

Sourcing and vetting crews/subcontractors; classification-risk-aware engagement structures as decision mechanisms; scope-of-work handoff to crews; inspection/walkthrough cadence and quality scoring; supplies/equipment responsibility models; backup coverage for crew failures.

Monthly margin health per contract (crew cost drift, scope creep, complaint load as mechanisms); the complaint-response system as the retention engine; contract renewals and repricing conversations; account expansion (frequency, add-on services, sister sites); when to exit an unprofitable contract.

businesses.label: Pest Control Sales / Referral Business
businesses.money_model: sell recurring pest-control service accounts (own licensed operation or commission/referral partnership with licensed operators); revenue = new-account commissions + recurring contract value
boundaries: pesticide application requires operator/applicator licensing - jurisdiction-specific and non-negotiable; unlicensed application is out of scope
door-to-door and neighborhood sales are regulated (permits, do-not-knock, cooling-off rules) - flag and respect
no infestation scare-selling; findings must be shown, not invented
commission structures as mechanisms, never invented figures

kbs.scope: Why route density is the economics of pest control (drive-time as the hidden cost mechanism); neighborhood/segment targeting; ethical door and referral selling with regulated-sales awareness; own-operation vs sell-for-operator models; seasonal demand waves.

The licensing/certification requirement classes for operators and applicators; partnering structures with licensed operators (who services, who owns the account); service-protocol literacy (inspection, treatment classes, IPM-style prevention framing) sufficient to sell honestly; safety and label-law respect.

Quarterly/monthly service-agreement mechanics; retention drivers (visible results, communication, easy scheduling); cancellation-save practice done ethically; seasonal add-ons (mosquito, rodent, termite-inspection classes) sold from need; account-book value in route-density terms.

businesses.label: Water Filtration Systems
businesses.money_model: sell/install whole-home or point-of-use water treatment; revenue = equipment + install + recurring filter-replacement/service plans
boundaries: no health scare-selling and no medical claims - water-quality findings must come from real, shown tests; claims limited to what treatment classes verifiably do
plumbing codes and (for some jurisdictions/products) contractor licensing are requirement classes to verify locally
in-home water demonstrations must be honest chemistry, not theater tricks presented as contamination proof
equipment margins and service-plan economics as mechanisms, never invented figures

kbs.scope: Segmenting by water problem class (hardness, taste/odor, specific-contaminant concerns) and geography; the honest diagnostic path (real test data, municipal water-quality reports, accredited-lab escalation); offer architecture (softener, carbon, RO classes as treatment mechanisms); ethical in-home selling rules.

Sizing to household demand and water chemistry as mechanisms; placement, bypass and drain requirements; plumbing-code and permit awareness (verify locally); install quality and leak-risk controls; commissioning tests and homeowner orientation; subcontract-plumber vs in-house models.

Consumables-annuity design (replacement schedules per treatment class as the recurring mechanism); service-plan tiers vs a-la-carte; reminder/scheduling systems that drive attach and renewal; water-retest cadence as proof of value; churn drivers and referral loops from visible water improvement.

businesses.label: Printer / Copier Leasing & Managed Print
businesses.money_model: place office print/copy equipment under lease + service contracts (cost-per-page); revenue = equipment placement + lease stream + per-page service contracts
boundaries: lease terms (evergreen clauses, buyouts, return conditions) must be disclosed plainly - the vertical's reputation problem is buried terms; this specialist encodes disclosure as a rule
per-page and lease economics as mechanisms, never invented rates
no overselling capacity a client's volume cannot justify

kbs.scope: Target segments still print-heavy (legal, medical, schools, logistics, municipal); dealer/manufacturer program models; the lease-sale conversation with plain-language term disclosure; competitive displacement timing around lease expirations; honest total-cost framing as mechanism.

Print-volume and workflow assessment (meter data over guesses); right-sizing device fleet to actual volume; delivery, network/scan integration and user setup; service-contract activation (coverage, consumables, response terms as mechanisms); baseline meter documentation.

The installed-base annuity: per-page service margins, consumable logistics and service-cost control as mechanisms; meter-read billing integrity; the lease-expiration calendar as the sales engine (upgrade vs extend vs return decisions); retention through uptime and honest renewals.

businesses.label: Office Coffee & Water Service
businesses.money_model: place coffee brewers/water systems in offices; revenue = equipment placement + recurring consumables (coffee, cups, filters) + service route
boundaries: route economics as mechanisms, never invented figures
food-handling/sanitation requirement classes verified locally
honest consumption-based proposals - no overstocking clients into resentment

kbs.scope: Office-coffee-service segments by headcount and culture; the free-trial/tasting acquisition play and its economics as mechanism; proposal design (equipment placement vs rental vs purchase models); displacement of self-serve retail buying; account qualification by consumption potential.

kbs.domain_label: Equipment Placement, Route Setup & Consumables Logistics
kbs.scope: Brewer/water-system selection per office size; placement, water-line and sanitation setup; consumables catalog and par-level design; route scheduling and vehicle/inventory logistics as the cost engine; service/cleaning cadence and equipment reliability.

Stop-level profitability (consumption volume vs service time as mechanisms); pricing and repricing consumables honestly; retention through reliability and stock-out prevention; expansion (snacks, water, breakroom supplies, micro-market class upgrades); route density growth and account-book value.

businesses.label: Travel Agent / Advisory Practice
businesses.money_model: book travel through host-agency or independent model; revenue = supplier commissions + planning fees + insurance/add-on commissions; repeat clients and referrals drive recurrence
boundaries: seller-of-travel registration classes exist in some states - verify jurisdiction before operating
travel-insurance selling may carry licensing/appointment requirement classes - verify before offering
commissions and host-agency splits as mechanisms, never invented percentages
honest expectation-setting on pricing vs online booking; no pay-to-play steering hidden from the client

kbs.domain_label: Agency Models, Host Agencies & Niche Selection
kbs.scope: Host-agency vs independent models (commission flow, support, consortium access as mechanisms); registration/compliance requirement classes; why niching (destination, trip type, clientele) drives supplier relationships and referrals; fee-model design (planning fees vs commission-only) and its client-alignment trade-offs.

Client discovery and trip design as the value product; supplier selection and relationship mechanics (preferred programs disclosed honestly); booking, documentation and payment-handling discipline; managing changes, disruptions and advocacy during travel; quality control that produces repeat clients.

Commission mechanics and payment timing as mechanisms (booked vs traveled); planning-fee capture; travel-protection/insurance add-ons offered under requirement-class awareness and honest fit; the repeat-and-referral engine (post-trip follow-up, trip-anniversary cadence); client-base value in a low-recurring vertical.

businesses.label: Solar Sales / Referral Business
businesses.money_model: commission per installed system (sales rep, dealer or referral model); weakest recurring potential in the set - the model is transaction commissions plus reputation-driven pipeline
boundaries: the vertical's reputation is damaged by high-pressure and misleading-savings selling - this specialist encodes anti-pressure, verified-numbers selling as identity, not garnish
savings/production claims must be mechanism-based (the client's own usage data, real rate structures, site production modeling) - never invented or guaranteed
financing/lease/PPA structures carry disclosure obligation classes; consumer-protection rules for door sales apply - verify jurisdiction
commission structures as mechanisms, never invented figures; installer licensing belongs to the installer

kbs.scope: Sales-rep vs dealer vs referral models and where commission risk sits (clawbacks on cancellation as mechanism); lead-generation channels and their cost/quality trade-offs; qualifying homeowners honestly (usage, roof, credit, motivation); the long sales cycle and pipeline math.

kbs.domain_label: Site Qualification, Proposal Integrity & Financing Literacy
kbs.scope: Site/usage qualification (consumption data, roof orientation/shade, utility rate structure as mechanisms); proposal integrity rules (production estimates from modeling, not promises; rate-escalator honesty); financing-structure literacy (cash, loan, lease/PPA classes) with disclosure-first explanation; permitting/interconnection process awareness.

Choosing installer partners on build quality and install backlog (the seller's reputation rides on the installer); handoff and install-timeline communication; cancellation/clawback management as mechanism; the referral engine from verified-happy installs; why reputation is this vertical's only durable recurring asset.
